program.title: Calisthenics Tracker
program.subtitle: A 12-week beginner calisthenics program
program.equipment_policy: Bodyweight only. Every session works with zero equipment; a pull-up bar is optional.
program.audience: True beginners and people returning to exercise

equipment_list.item: Floor space about 6 x 6 ft (2 x 2 m)
Heavy, sturdy table for rows (not folding or glass)
equipment_list.note: If you have no safe table, stay on doorframe rows.
Optional. Every pull level has a no-bar option.

phases.name: Foundation
phases.goal: Learn the movements, find your levels, build the habit.

phases.name: Build
phases.goal: More sets and slower lowering to build muscle and control.

phases.name: Strength
phases.goal: Harder levels with fewer reps, then retest in Week 12.

schedule.note: Any 3 non-consecutive days work (e.g. Tue/Thu/Sat). Leave at least one rest day between sessions. A 20-30 minute walk on rest days is encouraged but optional.

session_template.ramp_up_note: Before your first pair, do one easy set of 5 reps of each exercise one level easier.
session_template.pairing_note: Do the exercises in each pair back-to-back: one set of A1, rest, one set of A2, rest, repeat until all sets are done. Then move to pair B.

default_track._note: Suggested exercise for a typical true beginner in each phase. The user's own level (from the baseline test and level-ups) always overrides this.

special_sessions.title: Baseline assessment
special_sessions.note: Do the warm-up, then the baseline tests on the Assessment Sheet instead of a workout.

special_sessions.title: Week 12 retest
special_sessions.note: Do the warm-up, then repeat every test on the Assessment Sheet. Compare with Week 1.

progression_rules.title: Earn the next level
progression_rules.text: When you reach the TOP of the rep range on ALL sets with good form in two sessions in a row, move up one level next session. Start the new level at the bottom of the range.

progression_rules.title: Timed holds work the same way
progression_rules.text: Hold the top of the time range on all sets in two sessions in a row, then move up one level.

progression_rules.title: Too hard? Step down
progression_rules.text: If you cannot reach the bottom of the rep range on your first set with good form, drop one level (or use the 'Easier' option) for the rest of the session.

progression_rules.title: Leave reps in the tank
progression_rules.text: Stop each set when you have the week's target reps in reserve (RIR). Never train to failure in this program.

progression_rules.title: Form first
progression_rules.text: A rep only counts if it matches the form cues. If form breaks down, the set is over.

progression_rules.title: Deload weeks
progression_rules.text: In Weeks 4 and 8, keep your level, do fewer sets, and do not level up.

progression_rules.title: Missed sessions
progression_rules.text: Missed one session? Just continue. Missed a full week or more? Repeat the last week you completed. Never cram extra sessions.

progression_rules.title: Soreness check
progression_rules.text: Mild soreness for 1-2 days is normal. If soreness lasts more than 3 days or changes how you move, repeat the current week instead of moving on.

effort_scale.feel: Easy. Could do 4 or more extra reps.
Very hard. One good rep left.
Max effort. Not used in this program.

safety.disclaimer: This program is general fitness information, not medical advice. It is not a substitute for advice from a doctor or other qualified health professional. Talk to your doctor before starting any new exercise program, especially if you have a medical condition, an injury, are pregnant or postpartum, or have been inactive for a long time. You exercise at your own risk.
readiness_questions: Has a doctor ever said you have a heart condition or high blood pressure?
Do you feel pain in your chest at rest, during daily activities, or when you exercise?
Do you lose balance because of dizziness, or have you lost consciousness recently?
Do you have a bone, joint or soft-tissue problem that could be made worse by exercise?
Are you taking medication for a chronic condition, or has a doctor told you to limit activity?
safety.readiness_note: If you answer YES to any question, get clearance from your doctor before starting. Screening questionnaires such as the PAR-Q+ can help you and your doctor decide.
stop_signs: Pain that gets worse as you continue
normal_signs: Muscles burning near the end of a set
general_tips: Breathe out on the effort; never hold your breath.
Wear supportive shoes or go barefoot on a non-slip surface.
Test any chair, table, bench or bar before you put weight on it.
Clear the area of trip hazards and pets.
Drink water and stop if you feel unwell.

pull.intermediate: 8+ feet-elevated table rows or 3+ pull-up negatives

core.starter: Dead bugs or plank under 20 s

lateral_core.intermediate: 30 s side plank with leg lift

goal_options: Move and feel better day to day
next_steps: Repeat Weeks 9-12 at your new levels for another 4-week strength block.
Or restart the program at Week 5 using your new levels.
Keep climbing the ladders: stretch goals are full push-ups, decline push-ups, pull-ups and assisted pistols.
Add a fourth short session (core + mobility) if you have time and recover well.
Coming next: an Excel workbook with automatic level-up suggestions and progress charts.
